An algorithmic device is software that uses algorithms to calculate nonpublic competitor data in order to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels. Each month a landlord's use continues, and each residential rental property on which it is used, is a separate violation. Tenants may sue a landlord for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. A prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees, and lease provisions limiting fee recovery are unenforceable.
